items.name: pB2
items.direction: Narrate this as a high-energy, feel-good YouTube video comparing the GTA 6 game map with real Miami. The Narrator is THRILLED and grinning the whole time: an excited, fun friend who just found out how much Rockstar copied from Miami and is bursting to tell you. Huge smile you can hear in every line, bright and upbeat, warm and natural like real excited conversation, never like reading a script. Wide, lively pitch movement; real amazement on every number and reveal; playful delighted laughter in the voice on the funny bits (the lobster that turned into a whale, the 105 metres). The opening bet is a cheeky, confident challenge with a grin. Punch the key words with energy. Pace quick and bouncy, about 170 words per minute, short crisp pauses; never flat, calm, sleepy, monotone or documentary-serious, and never shouty or fake. Accent: native General American English, neutral American accent from first word to last. VOICE IDENTITY: the same person and the same high energy from the first line to the last. Say 'GTA six' as the letters G, T, A then 'six'. Pronounce 'Cortez' as 'cor-TEZ', 'Colon' exactly like the punctuation mark 'colon' (KOH-lun), never 'Colonna'. Pronounce 'Kaseya' as 'kah-SAY-uh', 'Clewiston' as 'KLOO-ih-stun', 'Okeechobee' as 'oh-kee-CHOH-bee', 'Leonida' as 'lee-oh-NEE-dah', 'Kalaga' as 'kah-LAH-gah', 'Belmar' as 'BEL-mar', 'Wynwood' as 'WIN-wood'. Read ONLY the text provided, word for word: stop right after the final sentence and never add, invent or continue with any words of your own. The text is given one sentence group per line: read every line in order, do not skip any line.
lines: The real one is the Kaseya Center, home of the Miami Heat.
In the game, it's the Sahara Arena, home of the Vice City Narcos.
Then, in 2026, a helicopter lowered giant pink letters onto the real arena's roof.
The county's price for that sign? 975,000 dollars.
Just 25,000 below the amount that would have needed a public vote.
But the game's most famous sign was copied from somewhere even stranger.
In the trailer, giant white letters spelling "VICE" stand at the end of the runway.
The real airport has no sign like that.
But for the movie Bad Boys, Hollywood built one there anyway. Giant letters spelling "MIAMI".
A movie prop... that became a video game landmark.
Now leave the city. Drive west. And the copying gets wilder.
In the game, they're called the Grassrivers.
That name comes from a 1947 book that called the Everglades a "River of Grass."
The book helped save the swamp. The same year, the Everglades became a national park.
The game's swamp has alligators, flamingos and airboats. Just like the real one.
It even hides Burmese pythons in the grass.
In the real Everglades, pythons are an invasive species. Pet snakes that escaped, and took over.
Head north from the swamp, and you hit something much sweeter.

lines: Stop eight. Clewiston, on Lake Okeechobee.
Florida's biggest lake. Surrounded by sugar cane.
Fans matched it to the game's Ambrosia. Its slogan: "Keeping Leonida Sweet."
The real sugar company becomes Allied Crystal. The lake becomes Lake Leonida.
Rockstar copied the town... and the sales pitch.
Now turn south. All the way south. To the end of the road.
A chain of islands, stitched together by bridges, like the Seven Mile Bridge.
In the game: the Leonida Keys. Same island chain. Same long bridge.
In the real Keys, a roadside village has a giant lobster. Nine metres tall. Her name is Betsy.
In the game, Betsy is gone. In her place: a giant whale.
Florida has islands, beaches, swamps and sugar. What it does not have... is mountains.
Florida's highest natural point is Britton Hill. Just 105 metres.
That's the lowest top point of any US state.
Plenty of Miami skyscrapers are taller than Florida's tallest hill.
But GTA six's Florida has a whole mountain national park.
Fans traced its canyons to Providence Canyon, in neighbouring Georgia.
So the copy has something the original doesn't.
And that's when the original started copying the copy.

lines: In 2026, Miami-Dade County pitched Rockstar a deal.
Rebrand the airport as "Vice City Airport."
Wrap the downtown trains. Put the game's logo on manhole covers.
The county sheriff pushed back. Her words: "Miami-Dade County is not Vice City."
But look up at the arena roof. Miami already says "Welcome to Vice City."

A hotel copied twice. Towers that are sinking. An apartment that's gone. Walls of murals. An arena with two names. A sign from a movie. A river of grass. A sweet town. A lobster turned whale. And mountains Florida never had.
Rockstar didn't build a fake Miami. It built a copy. And now Miami is dressing up as the copy.
So, which game should we put next to the real map? Tell us in the comments.
On this channel, we put the maps you think you know next to the real ones.
So if you want to see the next one, subscribe. It costs a lot less than a hundred-dollar bet.
See you on November 19th. In Vice City.
